business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business section
business_model.claim: CoreCivic provides corrections, detention, and residential reentry services to federal, state, and local government agencies, and is the nation's largest owner of partnership correctional, detention, and residential reentry facilities.
quotes: We are a diversified government solutions company with the scale and experience needed to solve tough government challenges in flexible, cost-effective ways.
Our customers primarily consist of federal, state, and local government agencies.
We are the nation's largest owner of partnership correctional, detention, and residential reentry facilities and one of the largest operators of such facilities in the United States.

business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2026, the company reports three operating segments: CoreCivic Residential (64 facilities, ~72,000 beds), CoreCivic Services (mail-order pharmacy, transportation, electronic monitoring), and CoreCivic Properties (five properties, ~8,000 beds).
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, through our CoreCivic Residential segment, we operated 64 correctional, detention, and reentry facilities, 56 of which we owned or controlled via a long-term lease, with a total design capacity of approximately 72,000 beds.

Through our CoreCivic Services segment, we provided mail order pharmacy services to over 600 correctional facilities, including correctional facilities owned or operated by CoreCivic, across 32 states, as well as transportation and electronic monitoring and case management services.
through our CoreCivic Properties segment, we owned five properties held for lease to government agencies, with a total design capacity of approximately 8,000 beds.

business_model.claim: In the Residential segment, CoreCivic is compensated at a per diem rate based on actual or minimum guaranteed occupancy levels, meaning revenue scales directly with the number of individuals housed.
quotes: we are compensated for providing bed capacity and correctional, detention, and residential reentry services at a per diem rate based upon actual or minimum guaranteed occupancy levels.

Through our CoreCivic Safety and CoreCivic Community segments, we are compensated for providing bed capacity and correctional, detention, and residential reentry services at a per diem rate based upon actual or minimum guaranteed occupancy levels.

The federal customers in our Residential segment generated 53% and 55% of our total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, increasing $71.3 million, or 22.2%, during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the same period in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P5 (funding amounts and dates) and P2 (non-traditional capacity risk).
growth_thesis.claim: For the ICE-driven growth to continue, federal immigration enforcement policy and dedicated funding must remain in place: OBBBA appropriates $75 billion to ICE and the Secure America Act secures an approximate $70 billion for DHS through September 30, 2029, but the evidence notes that ICE may use alternative capacity and that future administrations could restrict private detention.
quotes: OBBBA appropriates a total of $75 billion in mandatory funding to ICE for immigration enforcement activities and to increase detention capacity.

On June 10, 2026, President Trump signed into law an approximate $70 billion budget reconciliation bill, the "Secure America Act", which secures total funding to DHS for ICE and Customs and Border Protection, or CBP, through September 30, 2029.

ICE, the federal executive agency under the direction of DHS, has recently expanded its methods for physical detention by utilizing non-traditional detention capacity and by obtaining ownership of non-traditional facilities, and such methods could have an adverse impact on our business.

quotes: Patrick D. Swindle, the Company's President and Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"), has stepped down as President and CEO and resigned from his position on the Company's Board of Directors (the "Board"), effective as of September 24, 2026 (the "Transition Date"), due to health reasons.

Lucibeth N. Mayberry, who most recently served as the Company's Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer, has been appointed as President and CEO of the Company, effective as of the Transition Date.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Risk Factors and MD&A)
material_events.claim: ICE notified CoreCivic of its intent to terminate the IGSA for services at the 2,400-bed Dilley Facility, effective August 9, 2024, ending nearly ten years of operation.
quotes: On June 10, 2024, we received notice from ICE of its intent to terminate the IGSA for services at the 2,400-bed Dilley Facility effective August 9, 2024.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K MD&A)
material_events.claim: CoreCivic announced resumption of operations at the 2,400-bed Dilley Immigration Processing Center under an amended IGSA expiring in March 2030, with activation completed in September 2025.
quotes: On March 5, 2025, we announced that we had agreed under an amendment to an intergovernmental service agreement, or IGSA, to resume operations and care for up to 2,400 individuals at the 2,400-bed Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Dilley, Texas, or the Dilley Facility.
Activation of the Dilley Facility was completed in September 2025.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors), with renewal-rate counter from P1 (10-K Business)
risks.claim: 35 facility contracts representing $688.1 million (31% of 2025 total revenue) are scheduled to expire on or before December 31, 2026, of which 13 have no renewal options.
quotes: 35 of our facility contracts with the customers listed under "Business – Facility Portfolio" are currently scheduled to expire on or before December 31, 2026 but have renewal options (22), or are currently scheduled to expire on or before December 31, 2026 and have no renewal options (13).

The aggregate revenue earned during the year ended December 31, 2025 for the 35 contracts with scheduled maturity dates, notwithstanding contractual renewal options, on or before December 31, 2026 was $688.1 million, or 31% of total revenue.

risks.claim: After selling four detention facilities containing 7,187 beds to DHS for $2.2 billion, CoreCivic continues to manage them under existing ICE contracts that ICE can terminate for non-appropriation of funds or for convenience.
quotes: Sold four detention facilities containing 7,187 beds for gross proceeds of $2.2 billion
ICE has the ability to terminate the management contracts for non-appropriation of funds or for convenience.

We continue to manage the four facilities we sold to DHS under the existing management contracts with ICE. Although we and ICE have not yet modified the management contracts for these facilities to reflect the change in ownership, the range of our guidance incorporates our best estimate of the financial impact of the change in ownership.

risks.claim: ICE has expanded use of non-traditional detention capacity (military bases, soft-sided facilities, warehouse-based real estate, BOP facilities) and acquired its own real estate assets, which could divert occupancy from CoreCivic facilities.
quotes: ICE has increased its use of military bases (domestically and at Guantanamo Bay), soft-sided facilities, idled or under-utilized facilities owned and operated by the BOP, facilities owned by state and local government agencies, international options, and has most recently proposed using warehouse-based real estate, and has acquired certain real estate assets for use in ICE detention.

risks.claim: Legislation in California, Colorado, New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois, Oregon, and Washington prohibits state and local agencies from contracting to detain immigrants in ICE custody, restricting the customer base for CoreCivic's detention facilities in those states.
quotes: Legislation has been passed in California, Colorado, and New Jersey, where we operate detention facilities, as well as Maryland, Illinois, Oregon and Washington, that prohibits state and local agencies from contracting to detain immigrants in ICE custody.
